chunks: By the first chain, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yaqoub al-Sarraj, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was asked about faith, so he said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made faith upon four pillars: patience, conviction, justice, and jihad.'

So patience, from that, is upon four branches: longing, fear, asceticism, and vigilance. So whoever longs for Paradise disregards lustful desires; and whoever fears the Fire turns away from prohibitions; and whoever is ascetic in the world, hardships become easy for him; and whoever is vigilant of death hastens to good deeds.

And conviction is upon four branches: insight of intellect, interpretation of wisdom, knowledge of the lesson, and the way of the predecessors. So whoever has insight into intellect recognizes wisdom; and whoever interprets wisdom recognizes the lesson; and whoever recognizes the lesson recognizes the way; and whoever recognizes the way is as if he was with the predecessors, and he is guided to that which is most upright, and he looks at those who were saved by what they were saved by, and those who were destroyed by what they were destroyed by. And indeed, Allah destroyed those He destroyed due to their disobedience, and saved those He saved due to their obedience.

And justice is upon four branches: depth of understanding, vastness of knowledge, the blossom of judgment, and the garden of forbearance. So whoever understands interprets all knowledge; and whoever knows recognizes the laws of judgment; and whoever is forbearing does not neglect his affairs and lives among people praised.

And jihad is upon four branches: enjoining the good, forbidding the evil, truthfulness in the places, and hating the transgressors. So whoever enjoins the good strengthens the back of the believer; and whoever forbids the evil grinds the nose of the hypocrite and secures him from his plot; and whoever is truthful in the places fulfills what is upon him; and whoever hates the transgressors is angered for Allah; and whoever is angered for Allah, Allah is angered for him.
That is faith, its pillars, and its branches.
ai.seo_question: What are the four pillars and their branches of faith according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi presents a comprehensive taxonomy of faith, linking the four pillars of patience, conviction, justice, and jihad to specific spiritual states and practical actions. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the integration of inner belief (yaqin) with outward conduct (jihad), illustrating how intellectual understanding and moral discipline sustain the believer's journey. The detailed breakdown underscores the holistic nature of Iman, where theological certainty directly informs ethical behavior and social engagement.
